gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Mobile Pixels' own store prices the Trio 3 Pro at $509.99 today (2026-11-13; compare-at $599.99), $76.50 more than the $433.49 that ChatGPT's cards and our two pages show. Mobile Pixels also lists it for 15–16-inch laptops, while Macworld's review says 13–16-inch MacBooks.
standout_why: I read laptopbee.com (10 Best Triple-Screen Laptop Monitor Extenders) and masteritech.com (Best Laptop Screen Extenders 2026). Neither gives a price for any pick, apart from laptopbee's 'under two hundred dollars' for the ZUMWALT, and neither gives a total cost with a Mac adapter or dock. Macworld's how-to (675869) prices only docks and adapters, never an extender. ChatGPT's own cards and our pages show the Trio 3 Pro at $433.49 (and $469.23 at Storming Gravity), but the maker's price today is $509.99. No rival page gives a dated maker price or the fit conflict for the Trio.
decides: At $509.99 the Trio 3 Pro is no longer the cheap 1400p pick. It costs $120 more than the UPERFECT Z 14 at its $389.99 listing, which is from our 2026-11-10 page and was not rechecked today. Mobile Pixels sizes the Trio for 15–16-inch laptops, so it is a 15-inch Air pick at a higher price. That makes the 13-inch Air case for the Xebec Tri-Screen 3 stronger, even at $699 + $59 (not rechecked today). The KEFEYA S2Pro is the cheapest at $299.99, but it loses on an M1/M2/M3 Air: Kefeya says those Macs need a docking station, which costs extra.

findings.label: Laptop size per Macworld review
findings.value: 13- to 16-inch MacBooks; tested on a 14-inch MacBook Pro; 4.13 lb (1.9 kg); 300 nits per side screen; up to 65 W passthrough
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review | Macworld
findings.note: By Simon Jary, 2026-04-02, quoting $499.99 at launch. This conflicts with Mobile Pixels' own 15–16-inch listing. Macworld did not test it on a 13-inch Air.

findings.label: Software needed for both screens on a base-chip Mac
findings.value: Plain M1/M2 Macs and MacBook Neo need Mobile Pixels' free software (Simon Jary, Macworld)
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review | Macworld
findings.note: The review leaves out M3. Macworld's own how-to (next finding) says an M3 Air runs two externals only with the lid closed. So a lid-open M3 Air should be treated as needing the software too.

findings.label: MacBook Air external displays with the lid open
findings.value: M3 Air: two externals only with the lid closed. M4/M5 Air: two externals natively with the lid open. Plain M1/M2/M3 with the lid open need workarounds (DisplayLink-type software)
findings.source_title: How to connect multiple monitors to MacBooks (M1, M2, M3, M4 & M5) | Macworld
findings.note: This page names no screen extender and gives no extender price.

findings.label: Price at maker's US store
findings.source_title: KEFEYA S2Pro 2K 14-inch Laptop Triple Screen Extender
findings.note: Specs: 2 × 14" 2160×1440, 300 nits, 100% sRGB. Fit: '13-16.5"' in the title, '13"-17"' in the description. Why it loses: the page says 'For M1/M2/M3 MacBooks, a docking station is required' (dock not included), and it does not mention M4. Cheapest panel here, at $210 less than the Trio ($509.99 − $299.99).
